newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says 1997/98 budget to be higher.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says 1997/98 budget to be higher.

text.p: Indonesian Planning Minister Ginanjar Kartasasmita said on Monday the country's budget for 1997/98 (April-March) will be higher than fiscal 1996/97 but declined to give any figures.
"The budget must be higher but by how much we don't know yet. We are still calculating the figures," Ginanjar told reporters.
Indonesia 1996/97 budget showed a 16.1 percent rise to 90.6 trillion rupiah from 78 trillion rupiah the previous year.
Ginanjar predicted that in the 1997/98 budget the price of crude oil will not be below the price envisaged in the current budget of $16.50 per barrel.
He said the government will continue to be cautious on the current account deficit in the year to come.

Indonesia had estimated its current account deficit would widen to $8.7 billion in fiscal 1996/97 or about four percent of Gross Dometic Product (GDP), from $7.0 billion or about 3.2 percent of GDP in 1995/96.
